title: Almine Rech Shanghai presents Tia-Thuy Nguyen solo exhibition Fields of Resonance
summary: Almine Rech Shanghai is presenting ‘Fields of Resonance’, Tia-Thuy Nguyen’s third solo exhibition with the gallery, on view from August 28 to October 31, 2026. Cloudscapes are endlessly mutable. Yet observed from the same place over the course of a year, they reveal recurring patterns of their own. Much like climate, every place is marked by recurring patterns of cloud cover—dense or sparse, light or heavy, each season bringing with it a familiar sky. Towering cumulus clouds—a familiar presence in the skies of Vietnamese artist Tia-Thuy Nguyen’s hometown—occasionally appear in continental landscapes far drier than Vietnam. When they do, they can leave people, half in jest, wondering: Am I still here? Or have I somehow arrived in another city? title: Christie's to auction Chinese art from Art Institute of Chicago during Asian Art Week
summary: Asian Art Week returns to New York, bringing together exceptional museum and private collections that celebrate the enduring appeal of Chinese Works of Art over two live auctions and an online sale. Taken together, these auctions offer a singular opportunity for collectors, with hundreds of lots featuring works of great rarity, quality, and exceptional provenance. For more than a century, an exceptional collection of Chinese ceramics have remained in the care of The Art Institute of Chicago, their histories preserved through the vision and generosity of some of the most distinguished American collectors and philanthropists. Many works entered the museum in the early 20th century as landmark gifts and bequests from renowned patrons including Russell Tyson, Henry C. title: The broken family heirloom that inspired an entire art series
summary: A broken family heirloom might seem like the end of a story. For artist Rob Strati , it was the beginning of one. The first piece in Strati’s acclaimed Fragmented series began with something deeply ordinary: a piece of porcelain dinnerware that broke. The plate belonged to Barbara, Rob’s wife’s late mother. One day, it was accidentally dropped and shattered. But Strati couldn't simply throw the fragment away. He kept it, and at some point afterward, he picked up a pen and began working with what was left. That simple act became the foundation for Fragmented, an ongoing body of work in which Strati works with pieces of vintage porcelain, preserving their original decorative patterns while extending and transforming them through incredibly intricate ink drawings. title: Christoph Grunenberg appointed to Van Gogh Museum Supervisory Board
summary: Prof. Christoph Grunenberg, Director of Kunsthalle Bremen, has joined the Van Gogh Museum Supervisory Board. The museum is privileged to add an internationally renowned museum director and art historian with extensive governance and curatorial experience to its Board. Grunenberg has more than thirty years of international experience in the museum world. Before becoming Director of Kunsthalle Bremen, he was Director of Tate Liverpool and curator at Tate in London. He previously held positions at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, DC, Kunsthalle Basel and the Institute of Contemporary Art in Boston. Throughout his career, he organised numerous major international exhibitions and published extensively on modern and contemporary art. title: New book explores fashion and style of Marjorie Merriweather Post
summary: This fall, a new book opens the dressing room and jewelry vault of one of the most stylish women of her time, sharing a personal history of twentieth-century fashion and taste. The Fashion and Style of Marjorie Merriweather Post places the remarkable fashion collection of Marjorie Merriweather Post—hundreds of garments, jewels, and accessories from the late 19th century through the 1960s—within the broader story of American fashion, textile design, and decorative-arts culture. Published by Rizzoli Electa in partnership with Hillwood Estate, Museum & Gardens, the 200-page book, written by Megan J. Martinelli, Hillwood's curator of apparel, jewelry, accessories, and textiles, and featuring beautiful new photography by Alex Braun and Mark Finkenstaedt, along with a foreword by Kate Markert, Hillwood's executive director, will be released on September 8, 2026. title: TextielMuseum to open Hella Jongerius exhibition Smart hands
summary: This autumn, TextielMuseum opens the exhibition Hella Jongerius – Smart hands, offering a unique insight into the design process and textile archive of one of the Netherlands’ most influential designers. The exhibition follows Jongerius’ generous donation of her textile design archive to the museum. The archive comprises more than 4,000 sketches, models and material samples. In the exhibition, a selection from the archive is presented alongside realised textile products and objects. This reveals how Hella Jongerius’ work comes into being: the focus is not only on the final result, but also on the research, experimentation and making process behind it. Jongerius gained international recognition through designs for companies including IKEA, KLM, Vitra and Maharam. Her work is held in the collections of museums including MoMA in New York, the V&A Museum in London and Centre Pompidou in Paris. title: Christie's to present Kandinsky's 1907 masterpiece Das bunte Leben as a key highlight of upcoming 20/21 Evening Sale
summary: Christie's will present Wassily Kandinsky's, Das bunte Leben (1907) as one of the leading highlights of its 20/21 Marquee Frieze Week. This monumental canvas will be offered in the 20th/21st Century: London Evening Sale on 14 October 2026. Restituted to the heirs of Hedwig Lewenstein-Weyermannin in June 2023, Das bunte Leben is widely regarded as the defining achievement of Kandinsky's formative years and was exhibited to critical acclaim at the Salon d'Automne in Paris in the year it was created. During the years 1904–1908, the Parisian avant-garde was abuzz with new voices and experimental techniques, ushering in a dramatic new era of modern painting. Key exhibitions showcased the work of pioneering figures such as Paul Cézanne, Georges Seurat and Vincent van Gogh, as well as an array of different styles and movements, from Pointillism and Post-Impressionism to Fauvism

title: Edouard Kopp named director of the Johnson Museum at Cornell University
summary: Edouard Kopp, chief curator of the Menil Drawing Institute in Houston, has been named the next director of the Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art at Cornell University. He will begin his role as the Richard J. Schwartz Director on Nov. 1. In his seven years at the Menil Drawing Institute, part of The Menil Collection, Kopp oversaw administration, exhibitions, educational outreach and a collection of artwork from the 16th century to the present day. Prior to 2017, he held curatorial roles at the Harvard Art Museums in Cambridge, Massachusetts and at The J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles. “Edouard has a deep understanding of a university museum’s crucial role in teaching, research and public engagement,” Provost Kavita Bala said. “His commitment to expanding access to art, fostering interdisciplinary engagement and creating transformative experiences for audiences aligns closely with Cornell’s mission.” Kopp succeeds Jessica Levin

title: Grazer Kunstverein to highlight late conceptual artist Martin Maloney
summary: Grazer Kunstverein will present Martin Maloney, the first focused institutional presentation of the work of conceptual artist Martin Maloney (1938–2003). The exhibition will run from September 17 – December 13, 2026, opening on Friday, September 17, 2026 from 6–8pm. In New York City in the 1960s, when Conceptual art was taking shape, Maloney was there, standing next to the crib. He had a spot in Seth Siegelaub's 1966 "25 Show," was included in other influential group shows, and exhibited with Galerie Konrad Fischer. For a short while, he shared a studio with Lawrence Weiner on Bleecker Street. title: Zinedine Zidane's first ever wristwatch to be auctioned in Geneva
summary: ELA International (European Leukodystrophies Association) is pleased to announce the auction of Zinedine Zidane's first personal watch, a Cartier Pasha model, during the Rare Watches auction organised by Christie's on November 9, 2026, in Geneva. The sale will also host the charitable Watches For ELA auction, bringing together around twenty exceptional timepieces donated by leading watch brands and independent watchmakers. Proceeds from this sale will be donated to ELA International. This Cartier Pasha was the first watch Zinedine Zidane purchased for himself at the beginning of his professional career with FC Girondins de Bordeaux, giving it a particularly symbolic place in his personal journey. title: National Gallery opens call for 50 content creators to join digital network
summary: Following the success of the Gallery’s award-winning digital programme, an open call launches today for 50 UK-based content creators to join year three of the 200 Creators Network. The 200 Creators Network brought together a dynamic mix of digital voices to connect the nation’s paintings with new audiences. Spanning mudlarkers, BookTokers, photographers, fashion creators, florists and more, the Network brought the Gallery’s collection to life in fresh and unexpected ways. In total, the 2025/6 programme saw creator content reach over 10.8 million views and generate more than 260k engagements across social media. At the heart of the initiative were four Creative Collaborators - a small group of hand-selected creators who worked closely with the Gallery to co-create bold, original content. title: First full-scale Charley Harper exhibition coming to Cincinnati Art Museum
summary: The Cincinnati Art Museum is organizing its first full-scale, scholarly exhibition of works by Cincinnati art icon Charley Harper. The Art of Charley Harper: Creatures Wild and Tame, on view from October 16, 2026–March 7, 2027, will feature approximately 150 works by the beloved mid-century modern artist, designer, illustrator and nature advocate. The exhibition is presented in partnership with the Charley Harper Art Studio. “It’s hard to believe, but this is Charley’s first museum retrospective. Exhibition-goers can look forward to a special, historic treat,” according to studio director Brett Harper. “They will have the privilege to be able to see the 10 large paintings Charley completed on commission for the Interior Department’s U.S. National Park Service, which were only on public display in Washington, D.C., for a short time in the 1990s. title: Nakashima Foundation for Peace names Rachel Eichem Executive Director
summary: The Nakashima Foundation for Peace announced today that Rachel Eichem has been named to the new role of Executive Director. Eichem brings more than two decades of nonprofit leadership experience to the Foundation, with a career spent building philanthropic partnerships in the Delaware Valley, leading fundraising teams, and deepening community engagement on behalf of mission-driven organizations. Eichem most recently served as Executive Director for Pennsylvania and Delaware at Susan G. Komen Foundation, where she was accountable for a multi-million-dollar annual revenue target, provided oversight to the board and leadership council, and served as a spokesperson for the organization at press conferences and public events. title: Espoo Museum of Modern Art presents major survey of Howard Smith
summary: EMMA – Espoo Museum of Modern Art presents the long-awaited retrospective dedicated to Howard Smith (1928–2021). Best known for his printed fabrics for Vallila and ceramics for Arabia, Smith was also an exceptionally versatile artist who worked across painting, collage, papercuts, sculpture, textiles and public art. Bringing together around 90 works from 1965 to 2010, the exhibition reveals the breadth of Smith’s practice and his lasting impact on Finnish visual culture. Born in New Jersey, Howard Smith arrived in Finland in the early 1960s for what was intended to be a short visit. Instead, he made the country his home. Throughout a career spanning five decades, Smith was driven by curiosity and a constant openness to experimentation. title: rodolphe janssen to present Matthew Hansel solo booth at The Armory Show
summary: rodolphe janssen announced its sixth participation at The Armory Show in September 2026 with a solo project by Matthew Hansel (born 1977, Front Royal, VA, USA; lives and works in Brooklyn, NY, USA), who presents a series of new paintings. In his 1891 essay entitled, “The Critic as Artist”, Oscar Wilde wrote, “Man is least himself when he talks in his own person. Give him a mask, and he will tell you the truth.” Wilde asserts that people are unreliable narrators when restricted by the confines of selfhood. It is necessary then, that we find a way to subvert the self, so that we may be free from convention and express ourselves fully. It is the use of the mask (literal or figurative) that shields us and offers us protection from the world around us; from the norms, customs and mores of our time. title: Netherlands Open Air Museum seeks to document the working lives of contemporary sex workers
summary: The Netherlands Open Air Museum is turning its attention to a profession that has been part of society for centuries but remains largely absent from traditional museum collections: sex work. The museum in Arnhem has issued a call for contemporary sex workers willing to share not only the objects they use in their profession, but also the personal stories that surround their work. It is specifically looking for adults who receive clients in person while also working online through platforms such as OnlyFans, reflecting the increasingly hybrid nature of the profession. The initiative is part of the museum’s broader effort to document everyday life and work in the Netherlands for future generations. title: Aargauer Kunsthaus asks what creativity means in the age of artificial intelligence
summary: Can a machine be creative? And when artificial intelligence helps produce an image, a text or even an artistic decision, who can claim authorship? Those questions sit at the heart of Artificial Creativity, a new exhibition opening at the Aargauer Kunsthaus on September 26, 2026. Bringing together 14 artists and artist collaborations, the exhibition examines how artificial intelligence is entering the creative process — not simply as a new tool, but as a technology that is changing ideas about authorship, responsibility and even what society considers creative in the first place. On view through January 10, 2027, the exhibition comes at a moment when generative AI has moved remarkably quickly from a technological curiosity into everyday life. title: Kaiela Arts names Norm Yakaduna Stewart as 2026 Editions artist
summary: Kaiela Arts, an Aboriginal art centre located on Yorta Yorta Country in Shepparton, Victoria, has announced respected Kwat Kwat artist Norm Yakaduna Stewart as the artist for its 2026 Kaiela Arts Editions release, created in collaboration with Melbourne studio Spacecraft. Kaiela Arts Editions expands creative and commercial opportunities for First Nations artists, building on the success of the program’s inaugural edition in 2025 with internationally acclaimed artist Maree Clarke. The 2026 release features an exclusive limited edition of 40 hand-printed works on archival paper and 10 silkscreen prints on glass. title: Mark Feary announced as curator of the 2028 Adelaide Biennial of Australian Art
summary: The Art Gallery of South Australia today announces Mark Feary as curator of the 2028 Adelaide Biennial of Australian Art. Aotearoa New Zealand-born curator Feary brings more than twenty years of curatorial experience across contemporary art centres, universities, museums and artist-led initiatives, including his current position as Artistic Director of Gertrude Contemporary, Melbourne, and former roles at the Australian Centre for Photography, Sydney; Artspace, Sydney; Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Photography, Tokyo; Centre for Contemporary Photography, Melbourne; and West Space, Melbourne. Jason Smith, Director, Art Gallery of South Australia, said, ‘The Adelaide Biennial of Australian Art has been at the forefront of contemporary Australian art for 36 years, as the longest running survey of its kind. title: Belarussian artist Jura Shust explores spirituality and AI at Zachęta
summary: Jura Shust’s exhibition at the Zachęta – National Gallery of Art talks about topics related to the relationship between our spirituality and technology, and about the changing perception of nature in the contemporary world. The first solo presentation of the Belarussian artist in Poland, it guides viewers across landscapes such as borderland, ancient woodland, or a Christmas tree plantation. The artist has prepared a new multichannel installation especially for Zachęta, combining videos, sound, various items, and performative actions. The exhibition will be open for viewing between 17 July and 27 September 2026. The starting point for the exhibition is the borderland between Poland, Belarus, and Lithuania, where various traditions, languages, and belief systems have co-existed for centuries. title: Glenstone Museum debuts new Nick Cave commission this fall
summary: Glenstone Museum announced a new installation by Nick Cave (b. 1959). Opening Saturday, September 19, in Room 1 of the Pavilions building, the exhibition will be on view through spring 2028. Commissioned by Glenstone, Louder Still (2025) is the artist’s largest multi-figure Soundsuit to-date, gathering eleven discrete forms joined by a monolithic textile adorned with hand-sewn buttons made from iridescent mother of pearl shells. The oversized headpieces of each figure resemble gramophones or tuba horns, implying music and the sounds of protest, which Cave sees as integral to this body of work. The artist conceived the installation to be site-specific for Room 1. Installed directly on the building's terrazzo floor, the artwork will invite visitors to experience the sculpture in 360 degrees. title: The Sherborne to install Zak Ové's monumental sculpture assembly
summary: Thirteen monumental figures – each over two metres high - The Invisible Man and the Masque of Blackness (2016) will create a powerful encounter for visitors to the historic Georgian house. Ové’s immediately impactful installation explores the strength and resilience of the African diaspora, with its title referring to Ralph Ellison’s landmark novel Invisible Man and Ben Jonson’s Jacobean court entertainment The Masque of Blackness, first performed in 1605. The Sherborne presentation brings the figures together in a new formation, created specifically for the historic garden. The exhibition is co-curated by Liz Gilmore, CEO of The Sherborne, and Sir Robert Fry, former Chair of the Board of Trustees of The Sherborne House Trust 2018 (The Sherborne).
